definition_of_done: A Supabase migration creates session-scoped card storage with quadrant, ordering index, plain-text content, anonymous creator display name, creation/update timestamps and a nullable soft-deletion timestamp.

The Realtime bridge delivers an event caused by one connected client to another connected view of the same session in less than 2000ms from database commit to browser rendering, without polling; this is verifiable independently of the card-operation UI.
Realtime delivery does not send a session's card changes to views registered for another session.
Disconnecting the last view of a session releases its Realtime subscription.
Opening an existing session loads its persisted, non-deleted cards in deterministic quadrant order.
An anonymous participant can insert a plain-text card into a session quadrant, preserving their creator display name and server-generated timestamps.
A participant can edit a card's plain-text content without changing its original creator display name or creation timestamp.
A participant can soft-delete a card so that it disappears from connected canvases while its database record remains.
A participant can relocate a card to another quadrant and persist its target ordering index.
The initiating participant sees a pending card insertion or movement before its database request completes.
A rejected optimistic insertion or movement is removed or rolled back, respectively, with a visible failure indication.
Confirmed insert, edit, soft-delete and relocation operations are reflected in a second connected browser in less than 2000ms from database commit.
Card mutations reject references to a quadrant or card outside the specified session without modifying persisted state.
regression_guardrails: POST /sessions continues to return 201 with the existing response schema and a unique UUIDv4 session identifier for valid input.
Session creation continues to persist the initial quadrant structure.
POST /sessions continues to return 422 for missing or empty feature_name.
The existing /sessions/{session_id} page remains accessible for a valid session, including sessions with no cards.
The existing /sessions/{session_id} page continues to show a not-found message for an unknown session identifier.
Session creation continues to complete in less than 2000ms.
Adding card notifications does not suppress existing session/quadrant notifications on the shared Realtime delivery path.

SPEC.context:
Quadra already creates sessions and renders their quadrant canvases, but participants cannot yet collaborate through persisted cards. Realtime delivery was described in SPEC-0001 without an executable implementation commitment, leaving the central multi-user latency requirement unproved.

This change establishes the asynchronous Supabase-to-NiceGUI push bridge before the card UI depends on it, then adds session-scoped card persistence and anonymous insert, edit, soft-delete and relocation interactions. Connected participants receive confirmed changes without polling, while initiating participants receive immediate pending feedback.
api_contracts: Existing POST /sessions and GET /sessions/{session_id} retain their public contracts; no new public HTTP card endpoint is required.

Proposed src/quadra/cards.py in-process interface: list_cards(session_id), insert_card(session_id, quadrant_id, index, content, creator_display_name), update_card(session_id, card_id, content), soft_delete_card(session_id, card_id), relocate_card(session_id, card_id, quadrant_id, index). Mutations return the confirmed card or raise a typed validation/persistence error; client timestamps are not authoritative.

Proposed src/quadra/realtime.py asynchronous interface: register_view(session_id, view_id, callback) and unregister_view(session_id, view_id). Registration exposes subscription readiness; callbacks receive committed session-scoped changes.
Supabase Realtime Postgres Changes supplies committed card INSERT and UPDATE notifications; soft-delete is an UPDATE. Existing session/quadrant notifications remain supported.

Proposed src/quadra/canvas.py handles anonymous display-name entry and card interactions, applies Realtime callbacks within the appropriate NiceGUI view context, and uses NiceGUI WebSocket delivery to update browsers.
data_models: Proposed public.cards schema in supabase/migrations/0002_cards.sql: id UUID primary key, session_id UUID referencing the existing session relation, quadrant_id referencing the existing quadrant relation, index non-negative integer, content text, creator_display_name non-empty trimmed text, created_at timestamptz, updated_at timestamptz, deleted_at nullable timestamptz. The referenced relation names and quadrant-id type must be taken from supabase/migrations/0001_workspace.sql rather than invented.
Card identifiers are generated once per insertion and reused when reconciling optimistic and confirmed representations; this does not change UUIDv4 session identification.
Card timestamps are server-generated UTC instants. Creator display name and created_at remain unchanged by edits, relocation and soft-delete; updated_at records each mutation.
Active-card reads filter deleted_at IS NULL and order within each quadrant by index ascending, then card id ascending. Equal indexes are allowed; dense renumbering is not required.
Anonymous display names are per connected view, not user identities or access-control credentials. Card content and names are rendered as escaped plain text.
Pending browser representations are transient and keyed to the insertion identity or existing card id; Supabase remains the authoritative state.
dependencies: Existing session persistence in src/quadra/sessions.py and initial workspace schema in supabase/migrations/0001_workspace.sql.
Existing FastAPI/NiceGUI integration in src/quadra/api.py and src/quadra/app.py.
Available supabase-py asynchronous Realtime subscription API, running in the NiceGUI event loop.
Supabase Realtime publication configured for card changes and the existing session/quadrant notification sources.
Integration infrastructure capable of running Supabase and two actual browser clients, observing database commit and DOM-render timing.
needed_by: Concurrent quadrant-based team decision-making described by docs/strategy/STRAT-0002.md.
All card UI operations in this feature depend on the independently verified Realtime bridge.
constraints: Build and verify the Realtime bridge in its own increment before card UI increments depend on it.
Use Supabase async Realtime subscriptions and NiceGUI's existing WebSocket; do not introduce polling, direct browser Supabase subscriptions or a separate WebSocket gateway.
Use the stricter strategy target: database-commit-to-browser-render latency must be less than 2000ms, not merely less than or equal to it.
Measure latency with subscription readiness established and a common test timing reference; do not substitute callback receipt for browser rendering.
Load initial state after subscription readiness and reconcile notifications arriving during loading so a committed change is not lost between subscription and snapshot.
Scope reads, writes and notifications by session; any participant with the existing session link may edit its cards without introducing accounts.
Keep all persisted card fields authoritative on the server; do not add durable browser-side card storage.
Release subscriptions when no views need them, and preserve shared subscriptions while another registered view remains.
Plain-text cards only; cursor tracking, authentication, export and rich-text formatting remain out of scope.

The strategy supplies no quantitative concurrency or network-delay envelope; the less-than-2000ms acceptance check uses the declared integration fixture and is not a claim of an unlimited-load service-level guarantee.

decisions.text: We will route committed Supabase changes through an asynchronous, session-scoped Realtime service in the NiceGUI event loop and deliver browser updates over NiceGUI's existing WebSocket without polling.
decisions.title: Use one server-side push bridge for collaborative views
decisions.context: The approved architecture assigns subscription ownership to realtime-service, but the previous spec did not build or verify the bridge. Future collaborative features need a single established delivery path.
alternatives: Periodic database polling: rejected because it adds recurring reads and does not realize the selected push architecture.
Direct browser subscriptions: rejected because the approved architecture gives subscription ownership to the server-side Realtime service.
Separate WebSocket gateway: rejected for this increment because it changes the approved topology before the existing event-loop assumption has been tested.
positive_consequences: Future collaborative features can reuse session-scoped delivery and lifecycle management.
Browser delivery and the strict latency requirement receive an independent executable check.
negative_consequences: Long-lived asynchronous subscriptions require careful NiceGUI event-loop and disconnection handling.
The integration check requires live Supabase and browser infrastructure.

enforcement.rule: Committed changes reach a second same-session browser in less than 2000ms through Supabase Realtime and NiceGUI WebSocket with polling disabled.

decisions.text: We will make Supabase cards authoritative, enforce session ownership at the card-service boundary, and represent deletion with a retained row carrying deleted_at.
decisions.title: Persist authoritative session-scoped cards with soft deletion
decisions.context: Other features consuming cards must agree on ownership and deletion semantics; browser-local authoritative state would diverge across participants.
alternatives: Authoritative browser-local card storage: rejected because disconnected or concurrent views could disagree about persisted state.
Hard deletion: rejected because the strategy explicitly requires deleted cards to be hidden but retained.
Global card operations without a session parameter: rejected because they cannot enforce the session boundary consistently.
positive_consequences: Reloads and connected views share a durable source of truth.
Deleted card records retain their authorship and temporal data.
negative_consequences: Retained deleted rows consume storage and every active-card read must filter them.
Session validation adds checks to every card mutation.

enforcement.rule: Cross-session card mutations leave persisted state unchanged, and soft-delete retains the row while excluding it from active-card reads.

decisions.text: We will show transient optimistic insertion and relocation states, reconcile them by card identity after confirmation, and remove or roll them back on persistence failure.
decisions.title: Use optimistic feedback for insertion and movement
decisions.context: The initiating participant should see their operation without waiting for a persistence round trip.
alternatives: Wait for persistence before rendering: rejected because it cannot guarantee visible feedback while a request is pending.
positive_consequences: Insertion and movement remain visibly responsive while persistence is pending.
negative_consequences: The canvas must maintain transient pending state and implement rollback.

architecture_change.summary: Add card persistence and an asynchronous Supabase-to-NiceGUI event bridge, with explicit cross-client push acceptance criteria under 2000ms.

added.name: Card Service
added.owns: Loads session-scoped cards and persists insert, update, soft-delete and quadrant relocation operations, including ordering, anonymous display-name authorship and timestamps.
added.does_not_own: User authentication, durable browser-side state or delivery of Realtime events to connected clients.

added.name: Realtime Synchronization Service
added.owns: Maintains asynchronous Supabase Realtime subscriptions within the NiceGUI event loop, routes database change notifications to connected views of the affected session, and manages subscription lifecycle and cleanup.
added.does_not_own: Card persistence, cursor tracking or a separate WebSocket gateway.

added.name: Collaborative Canvas
added.owns: Renders session cards, captures anonymous display names and card operations, provides optimistic or quick-confirm feedback for the initiating participant, and applies confirmed changes to connected browser views through NiceGUI.
added.does_not_own: Authoritative card storage, user accounts or direct browser subscriptions to Supabase.

relations_added.description: Calls in-process to load session cards and request insert, update, soft-delete and relocation operations.
Reads and writes session-scoped card records using supabase-py; committed mutations are the source of Realtime events.
Registers and unregisters connected session views for push delivery as clients connect and disconnect.
Pushes committed card changes and existing session/quadrant change events over asynchronous Supabase Realtime subscriptions, without polling.
Dispatches session-scoped database changes in-process; the canvas updates connected browsers through NiceGUI's WebSocket without polling.

relations_removed.description: Pushes Realtime change events on sessions and quadrants; quadra-app forwards them to browsers over NiceGUI's WebSocket.
